$schema.description: The JSON Schema editors validate this file against.

lenses.description: Commands the reader can look at a document through.

ColorTheme.description:
One of GitHub's colour themes.

The names are GitHub's own, and each has a matching block of Primer design
tokens in the frontend stylesheet keyed by exactly this string, so a
variant renamed here renders as no theme at all.

GitHub also ships a high-contrast pairing for the dimmed and colour-vision
themes, applied when the operating system asks for increased contrast.
Those are not offered as choices, here or on GitHub.

DirectoryConfig.description:
Where the file tree is rooted when the app starts.

There is no `onNewWindow` here: which folders a new window starts with is
decided by the command that opened it — Cmd+N carries the places alone,
Cmd+Shift+N duplicates this window's temporary roots as well — rather
than by a setting that has to guess between them.

defaultDirectory.description:
The folder the first window works in, beside the places. `None` starts
with the places alone.

FileOpenBehavior.description: Behavior for routing externally opened files/directories.

oneOf.description: Always create a new window.
Open in the last focused visible window when possible.
Open in a visible window on the cursor's current screen when possible.

Lens.description:
A command the reader configured to look at a document through: its
answer is shown with the document, which itself is never changed.

agent.description:
The agent to run, which Arto knows how to call and to read; without
one, `command` is run instead.

allow.description:
What the agent may do beyond reading the text it is handed; nothing
when empty.

apiKeyCommand.description:
A program and its arguments that print the server's API key — a
password manager — in place of the key Arto keeps in the system's
credential store for the endpoint. Neither is written into the
configuration.

command.description:
Program and arguments of a command that is not a known agent, run as
they are, without a shell.

concurrency.description: How many per-block runs may be in flight at once.

context.description: How many blocks on each side a per-block run is handed as context.

contextLength.description:
Ollama: the context the model is loaded with, in tokens; sized to
each request when absent. Ollama otherwise loads a model with the
longest context it takes, which for some models means tens of
gigabytes of memory.

endpoint.description:
The server's base URL. Ollama: its address, `http://127.0.0.1:11434`
when absent. OpenAI: the part before `/chat/completions`, such as
`https://api.openai.com/v1`.

id.description: Unique among the lenses; also what cached answers are filed under.

model.description: The model the agent uses; its own default when absent.

on.description:
What the lens is offered to look at. A `page` lens takes the
document's places, so it looks at a whole document whatever this
says, and cannot be set to a block.

program.description: Where the agent's program is, when it is not found on its own.

prompt.description:
What the agent is asked to do with the text it is handed. Without one
the agent is handed the text alone, which is what a model trained for
a single task — a translation model — expects: it reads any
instruction as more text to work on.

shortcut.description:
The keys that show or hide the lens over the document, written as the
keybindings are: `Cmd+Shift+t`, or `g t` for one chord after another.

system.description:
The system prompt a server is given with every request. A model
trained for a single task may read its settings from it — the language
to translate into, say.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long one run may take before it counts as failed.

unit.description: How a `page` lens hands the document over.

LensAgent.description:
Something Arto knows how to ask and how to read the answer of: the lens
gives it a prompt instead of a whole command.

oneOf.description: The `claude` command-line agent.
The `codex` command-line agent.

An Ollama server, through its own API, which unlike its
OpenAI-compatible one takes the context length with each request.
A server with an OpenAI-compatible chat completions API.

LensCapability.description:
Something an agent is kept from unless the lens allows it.

An agent is run as a plain text transformer by default, because the
document it is handed can talk it into anything its tools can do. What a
lens allows is the reader's decision for that lens; it is never implied.

oneOf.description:
Search the web and read what it finds, which a fact check needs.
What leaves the machine is what the agent was already handed.
Read the files around the document.

Run commands. The agent's own sandbox, where it has one, still
keeps them from writing.

LensDisplay.description:
How much of the document a lens hands its command, and where the answer
is shown.

oneOf.description:
One run per block, with its neighbours as context; each answer is
kept beside its block and shown on hover — an explanation, a gloss.

One run over the document or the block, and one answer, shown on
request — a summary.

One run over the whole document, whose answer is a document of its
own, shown in place of the page as it arrives — a translation.

LensTarget.description:
What a lens is offered to look at: some questions are about one block —
explain this paragraph — some only make sense of a whole — summarize it —
and some fit either.

oneOf.description: The block a right-click marks, or the keyboard cursor is on.
The whole document.

LensUnit.description: How much of the document one run of a `page` lens is given.

oneOf.description:
The whole document in one run, which a general model translates
best: it sees every part of what it is translating.

Each of the document's top-level blocks in a run of its own, which
is what a model trained on sentences and paragraphs — a small
translation model — handles: handed a whole document, it drops and
merges blocks.

NewWindowBehavior.description: Behavior when opening a new window

oneOf.description: Use the default setting
Use the setting from the last focused window

OpenFromPanel.description:
What the panel does once a document has been opened from one of its rows.

Two readings of the same list, and both are ordinary. One reader keeps the
panel out and works down it, opening a document after a document; the other
goes to it to fetch one thing and wants the page to themselves once they
have it.

oneOf.description: The list stays where it is.

The panel puts itself away, leaving the document alone on screen. A
pinned panel unpins: what was asked for is the document by itself.

RawHtml.description:
What becomes of raw HTML written into the Markdown. A document may embed markup the Markdown syntax cannot say — a ``, a `
`, an `` with a width — and passing it through is what makes that work. The same passthrough lets a `

oneOf.description: Write every raw HTML node through untouched.

GFM's tagfilter: neutralize the tags that restyle or script the page
(`<style>`, `<script>`, `<iframe>` and friends) by escaping their
leading `<`, and leave all other markup working.
Escape every raw HTML node, so the document shows its own markup.

RecentTrace.description:
When the margin trace — the documents read before this one, left at the
edge of the page — is drawn.

It is the one window on the history nobody asks for, which is why it is
the one that can be turned off. Whatever is chosen here, the trace is
drawn only where there is a margin to draw it in: a window too narrow to
keep the document readable hides it, and so does a document set to the
full width, which leaves no margin at all. That is state, not a change to
this setting.

oneOf.description: Never drawn.
Hidden while the panel is out, since it already lists documents.

Always drawn, where there is a margin for it.

`hidden_when_full_width` is the old name of this: it named a choice
that is now simply what happens, since a document at full width has no
margin for the trace to be in. A configuration that still says it
keeps working and means this.

RenderOptions.description:
Choices that change how Markdown is rendered.

This is also the `markdown` section of Arto's `config.json`, so every
consumer of the pipeline (the app, `arto page`, Quick Look) exposes the
same options and reads the same user preferences. The struct carries
`#[serde(default)]`, so a configuration file naming one option gets the
documented default for every other.

The GFM baseline — tables, task lists, strikethrough, footnotes — is not
here. Those constructs are what a Markdown document written for GitHub
contains, and a reader that renders them as literal pipes and brackets is
broken rather than configured. What is here is the layer above that
baseline, where a construct's syntax collides with prose somebody actually
writes: `$5 and $10` is not a formula, and `[[a]]` is not always a link.

cjkEmphasis.description:
Let emphasis pair when its delimiters sit against East Asian
punctuation, so `**強調。**` is emphasized.

CommonMark's flanking rules read the punctuation on either side of a
`*` run to decide whether it may open or close, and East Asian
punctuation blocks the run the way Latin punctuation does — except
that CJK text sets punctuation directly against the words, where Latin
text puts a space in between. Off is what GitHub renders.

definitionLists.description: Read PHP Markdown Extra / mdBook definition lists.

headingAttributes.description:
Read a trailing `{#id .class}` on a heading as the id and classes to
render it with, rather than as part of its text.

headingPermalinks.description: Append a `#` link to each heading, the way GitHub does.

math.description:
Read `$…$` and `$$…$$` as formulas for the math renderer.

Off leaves a document that writes `$` for something else alone: two
shell variables in one line (`echo $HOME/$USER`) otherwise pair up
into a formula spanning both.

rawHtml.description: What becomes of raw HTML written into the Markdown.

smartPunctuation.description: Replace quotes, dashes and ellipses with their typographic forms.

subscript.description:
Read `~text~` as subscript.

Off keeps a lone `~` literal, which is what a document using tildes
for approximation (`~5 minutes`) means by it.

wikiLinks.description: Read `[[target]]` and `[[target|label]]` as links to another document.

defaultPinned.description: Whether sidebar is pinned to the layout by default

defaultShowAllFiles.description: Whether to show all files (including non-markdown) by default

defaultZoomLevel.description: Default zoom level for sidebar content

minContentWidth.description:
The width the document keeps while anything else can give way instead.

Every threshold in the layout is this number plus the width of what
is still drawn beside the document, so raising it folds the trace,
the panel, the gutter and the rail at correspondingly wider windows.

Theme.description:
The user's theme preference.

`Auto` follows the operating system; resolving it to light or dark is the
app's job, since it needs the system appearance.

ThemeConfig.description:
Configuration for theme-related settings

`lightTheme` and `darkTheme` carry their own defaults because a
configuration written before they existed omits them, and because the dark
slot defaults to something other than [`ColorTheme::default`].

darkTheme.description: Which of GitHub's themes to paint in dark mode

lightTheme.description: Which of GitHub's themes to paint in light mode
